LESSON: READING 13.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: INDEPENDENT READING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 13
Topic 13.2: Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading, part of Strand 13 in Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: where they meet on a regular basis to read books and do extensive reading activities. 1. Why is it important to read newspapers and magazines?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read newspapers, magazines and articles,

2. select and read age-appropriate and high-interest materials from print and electronic sources related to the theme,

3. infer the meaning of words related to the theme,

4. retell the stories they have read in groups,

5. share opinions and reflect on the materials they have read,

6. set up an after-school club offline or online

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read newspapers, magazines and articles,
2. select and read age-appropriate and high-interest materials from print and electronic sources related to the theme,
3. infer the meaning of words related to the theme,
4. retell the stories they have read in groups,
5. share opinions and reflect on the materials they have read,
6. set up an after-school club offline or online

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: This is enhanced when the learner sets up after-school clubs for reading purposes.

• Learning to Learn: This is achieved as the learner develops independent reading skills that enable them to look for

information on their own.

Values:
Responsibility: This is nurtured as the learner offers leadership and guidance to others while preparing to play the telephone

game.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Financial Literacy: It is nurtured as the learner interacts with reading materials on money.

Problem solving skills for better living: The learner reads stories on how people handle money and the consequences

of that.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can ably link extensive reading to other subjects such as Kiswahili which have such concepts taught and

encouraged.
